deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of a systematic exposition, §5 'Classes remarquables d'opérateurs dans l'espace de Hilbert', of Schatten's theory of symmetric norming functions and the operator ideals they define. The page continues the construction begun on the previous page.

(i) Smallest extension. Let N_0 be a 'Schatten norm' on R^n: symmetric, depending only on |x_i|, monotone on the positive cone, and normalised by N(e_1)=1. For x in c_0, let ρ_1(x) ≥ ρ_2(x) ≥ ... be the decreasing rearrangement of the |x_i|. Set N(x) = N_0(ρ_1(x), ..., ρ_n(x)).
- Homogeneity and definiteness are trivial.
- Monotonicity forces any symmetric monotone extension to dominate this N, so N is the smallest extension.
- For the triangle inequality, G. passes to operators. Let u_x be the diagonal operator on l^2 with entries x, so its singular values are ρ_i(x) and f(u_x) = f(x). Then u_{x+y} = u_x + u_y, and the inequality follows from 'No 4, th. 4, corollaire'. That is presumably the Ky Fan / Weyl-type result that a symmetric gauge function of the singular values is subadditive (Ky Fan dominance).

(ii) Correspondence. This gives a correspondence between 'Köthe' (formerly 'Schatten') norms on R^n and those Köthe norms on R^(N) that are 'induced by c_0'.

(iii) The space l^N. Given a Köthe norm N on R^(N) and an arbitrary sequence x, set |x|_n = (|x_1|, ..., |x_n|, 0, ...). This sequence of positive vectors increases with n, so define N(x) = lim_n N(|x|_n), a value in [0, ∞]. It agrees with N on R^(N).
- Homogeneity holds, with care about the convention 0·∞ when λ=0.
- Subadditivity: |x+y|_n ≤ |x|_n + |y|_n, so by monotonicity N(|x+y|_n) ≤ N(|x|_n + |y|_n) ≤ N(|x|_n) + N(|y|_n).
- Hence l^N = {x : N(x) < ∞} is a normed sequence space.
- The next page shows l^1 ⊂ l^N ⊂ l^∞ with injections of norm ≤ 1.

This is the standard construction of symmetric (Banach) sequence spaces. It serves as the prelude to defining the operator ideals S_N = {u compact : (s_i(u)) ∈ l^N}.
errors: No real error. The appeal to the operator inequality (No 4, th. 4) is heavier than needed. For diagonal operators the needed fact is just the weak majorization ρ(x+y) ≺_w ρ(x)+ρ(y), together with the monotonicity of symmetric norms under weak majorization, which can be proved directly.
The 0·∞ convention for λ=0 in N(λx) = |λ| N(x) has to be handled separately; the page notes this.

ideas.what: Minimal symmetric extension of a symmetric gauge norm from R^n to finitely supported sequences via the decreasing rearrangement
ideas.modern_name: symmetric norming function / truncation to the n largest singular values (Ky Fan-type norms)
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck, Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), and Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955) on rearrangements and convexity inequalities

ideas.what: Triangle inequality proved by embedding sequences as diagonal operators and invoking a Ky Fan/Weyl singular-value inequality
Extension of a symmetric norm to all sequences by monotone limits, giving the space l^N between l^1 and l^∞
ideas.modern_name: symmetric (rearrangement-invariant) sequence space / Köthe sequence space with the Fatou property

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard textbook development of symmetric sequence spaces underlying Schatten ideals. The only minor curiosity is the terminology shift from 'norme de Schatten' to 'norme de Köthe'.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: '(soit ...' appears to be '(cf. ... = pour x,y ∈ (c_0))' with 'soit' struck through. The reading is uncertain.
The fragment 'on a f(u_x) = f(x)' likely reads 'f_i(u_x) = f_i(x)' (singular values ρ_i), not a single f.
In the main text the word 'Schatten' is systematically replaced by 'Köthe' (e.g. 'normes de Köthe', with 'de Köthe' inserted above the line).
